package_info.package_name: tkcalendar (example, applies to all listed typosquatted packages)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is malicious because it is part of a large-scale typosquatting campaign targeting users who mistype popular package names. Every package contains obfuscated Python code that, upon installation, deploys a malicious browser extension designed to hijack the clipboard and replace copied cryptocurrency wallet addresses with attacker-controlled addresses, enabling theft of cryptocurrency.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated Python code with variable names in Chinese (e.g. 馬女水女口目人馬鳥月水馬山山馬鸟) that, when deobfuscated, writes a browser extension to %APPDATA%\Extension and modifies browser shortcuts.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code writes a malicious browser extension to %APPDATA%\Extension and modifies browser shortcuts in Windows Start Menu and Taskbar to load the extension on browser launch, enabling persistent malicious behavior.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes on install, writes files outside the package directory, and tampers with system browser shortcuts, which is not expected for any legitimate Python package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not modify browser shortcuts or install browser extensions, especially not via obfuscated code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise deployment tools may modify shortcuts, but never in this context or with obfuscated code.
key_indicators: Modifies browser shortcuts to inject extension

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At browser launch, the extension requests clipboard access and active tab permissions, enabling it to monitor and modify clipboard contents.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A browser extension installed outside the official store and requesting clipboard access is highly suspicious, especially when deployed by a Python package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Python packages do not install browser extensions, and legitimate extensions are not deployed this way.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Clipboard managers or password managers may request similar permissions, but are installed via user consent and official channels.

execution_context.trigger: clipboard event (user copies text in browser)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user copies a string matching a cryptocurrency wallet address, the extension replaces it in the clipboard with an attacker-controlled address, enabling redirection of funds.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting clipboard events and replacing wallet addresses is a classic clipboard hijacking technique, which is always malicious outside of explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate extensions do not silently replace clipboard contents with attacker-controlled data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Clipboard managers may modify clipboard, but not to redirect funds.
key_indicators: Regular expressions for crypto wallet addresses

attack_chain.action: User installs a typosquatted malicious package from PyPI.
Malicious Python code executes on install, writes browser extension files to %APPDATA%\Extension, and modifies browser shortcuts to load the extension.
attack_chain.leads_to: Browser launches with malicious extension loaded

attack_chain.action: Browser extension requests clipboard and activeTab permissions via manifest.json.
attack_chain.leads_to: Extension can monitor and modify clipboard

attack_chain.action: When user copies a crypto wallet address, background.js replaces it with an attacker-controlled address.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim's funds are redirected to attacker if pasted into a transaction

behavioral_signatures: Python package executes code on install that writes files outside its own directory
Modification of browser shortcuts to include --load-extension argument
Installation of browser extensions outside official extension stores
Clipboard event interception and replacement of cryptocurrency wallet addresses
file_indicators: Obfuscated Python files with Chinese variable names
network_indicators: No direct C2, but attacker wallet addresses as IOCs (e.g., 0x6eb2103839011Ed56c98145b3d3f9d6BE1b4dA63, bc1qkjm7r677a4fkxcmx9kzlk55a9eaqtztq8zwrc2, etc.)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that execute code on install and write to %APPDATA%\Extension or modify browser shortcuts. Detect browser shortcuts with --load-extension arguments pointing to non-standard locations. Scan for browser extensions installed outside official stores, especially those with clipboard permissions and code matching known clipboard hijacking patterns. Flag clipboard event handlers in extensions that use regexes for crypto wallet addresses and hardcoded replacement values.
